events.verdict: Cunningham's (DET) hand slides off the ball and initiates illegal contact with Allen's (CLE) arm during the post shot attempt.
Duren (DET) extends his arms toward Merrill (CLE) during the screen, and the contact is marginal.
Allen (CLE) initiates contact with Thompson's (DET) body, affecting the shot attempt.
Duren's (DET) hand slides off the ball and initiates contact with Allen's (CLE) wrist, affecting his ability to make his intended pass. The illegal contact causes the errant pass.

Replay review of the foul called on Tyson (CLE) pursuant to a coach's challenge was deemed successful. Prior to Tyson delivering contact that dislodges Robinson (DET), Robinson grabs and pulls Tyson's jersey, affecting his FOM. Because the contact occurs prior to the throw-in, an away from the play foul is assessed.
Sasser (DET) immediately slides his hand off of Mobley's (CLE) body as he cuts down the lane, and the contact is marginal.
Duren (DET) maintains a legal guarding position alongside Schroder's (CLE) path as he defends the shot attempt.
The loose ball bounces off of Duren (DET) as he is standing out of bounds and possession correctly remains with Cleveland.
Schroder (CLE) releases from Jenkins (DET) as he spins away from him during the drive, and the contact is marginal.

Duren (DET) and Allen (CLE) each make clean contact with the ball while pursuing the rebound. Allen is the last player to touch the ball before it goes out of bounds, and possession is correctly awarded to Detroit.
Allen (CLE) grasps and immediately releases Duren's (DET) arm during the throw-in, and the contact is marginal.
Allen (CLE) makes contact with the ball and legally blocks Duren's (DET) shot attempt at the basket.
Thompson (DET) slips and falls on his own, and there is no illegal contact by Tyson (CLE) as they move up the court.
Duren (DET) legally contests Schroder's (CLE) driving shot attempt.

Mobley's (CLE) left hand grazes Jenkins' (DET) head as he raises it to contest the shot at the basket, and the contact is marginal. Contact to an opponent's head/face can be deemed marginal when the result of a natural basketball move, provided the contact is not disproportionate or uncontrolled.
Schroder (CLE) is the last player to touch the ball before the ball goes out of bounds. Possession correctly remains with Detroit.
Tyson (CLE) legally contests Sasser's (DET) jump shot attempt.
Harris (DET) and Merrill (CLE) mutually engage and marginal contact occurs as they jostle for rebounding position.
After the pass is deflected, Jenkins (DET) and Schroder (CLE) converge on the same spot in pursuit of the loose ball, and the contact is incidental.
Schroder (CLE) legally contests Jenkins' (DET) jump shot attempt.
Thompson (DET) immediately slides his hand off of Porter Jr.'s (CLE) back and marginal contact occurs during the throw-in.
Jenkins (DET) rests his hands on Merrill's (CLE) side as he moves in the same direction toward the sideline, and the contact is marginal.
Jenkins (DET) is the last player to touch the ball before the ball goes out of bounds. Possession correctly remains with Cleveland.
Thompson (DET) initiates contact with Porter Jr.'s (CLE) arm and the contact affects his SQBR.
Sasser (DET) cleanly dislodges the ball from Tyson (CLE) and Tyson is the last player to touch the ball before it goes out of bounds. Possession should be awarded to the Pistons.
Harris (DET) commits a take foul on Mobley (CLE).
Tyson (CLE) commits a take foul during Jenkins' (DET) upward shooting motion, and a shooting foul is correctly assessed.
Duren (DET) and Thompson (DET) both make clean contact with the ball to block Schroder's (CLE) driving shot attempt. The ensuing follow-through contact after the block is considered incidental.
There is no clear and conclusive video evidence to determine whether Merrill (CLE) makes contact with Jenkins' (DET) arm or the ball first while deflecting the pass at the end of the drive.
Robinson (DET) grabs and holds Porter Jr.'s (CLE) right arm, which affects his FOM off-ball.
Sasser (DET) briefly grasps and releases Merrill's (CLE) arms as they approach Mobley's (CLE) legal screen, and the contact is marginal.
Jenkins (DET) maintains a legal guarding position as he defends Schroder (CLE) at the end of the drive.
Porter Jr. (CLE) makes clean contact with the ball and deflects it away from Sasser (DET) as the steal occurs.

Replay review of the foul called on Jenkins (DET) pursuant to a coach's challenge was deemed successful. Jenkins makes clean contact with the ball to block Porter Jr.'s (CLE) driving shot attempt. The ensuing arm follow-through contact after the block is deemed incidental. At the time of the whistle, Jenkins has imminent possession of the ball and Detroit is correctly awarded possession after the successful challenge.
Mobley (CLE) is in the paint for less than three seconds when the shot is imminent.
Tyson (CLE) legally contests Harris' (DET) post shot attempt.
Duren (DET) is the last player to touch the ball before the ball goes out of bounds.
Sasser (DET) and Merrill (CLE) briefly engage and disengage as they navigate the screen.
Sasser (DET) makes clean contact with the ball and temporarily dislodges it from Merrill (CLE) during the steal attempt.
Duren (DET) makes clean contact with the ball and deflects it away from Mobley (CLE) prior to incidental follow-through arm contact occurring.

Duren (DET) raises his arms for a potential rebound and inadvertent contact occurs with Merrill's (CLE) head/face as the ball goes through the basket.  Contact to an opponent's head/face can be deemed marginal when the result of a natural basketball move, provided the contact is not disproportionate or uncontrolled.
Sasser (DET) contests Merrill's (CLE) jump shot attempt and initiates illegal lower-body contact following the release of the shot attempt.
Merrill (CLE) commits a take foul on Sasser (DET).
Merrill (CLE) makes clean contact with the ball to tie it up with Sasser (DET), and a jump ball is correctly called.
Harris (DET) legally contests Mobley's (CLE) jump shot attempt.
